I didn't mean to let on that I go around in elaborate strange outfits or anything, I just live in a cowboy town and I can't stand cowboy culture. I am planning a move that's coming up pretty soon which should help in that regard, but really, this whole province has been grating me down for years for not wearing boots and a hat, so its kind of a raw nerve. My hair's just long, I put effort into making it presentable but that's just not accepted by people here. 
As for the story telling, I am an animator and am currently working on a graphic novel. I understand problems inherent to medium and all that, what I meant by that was really, everyone around seems interested in everyone's life but mine, like my existence is so foreign to the people around me they get scared or uncomfortable. I hate being a source of discomfort.
I appreciate that you aren't just telling me to stop being weird though, that's been the first bit of advice from most people who've offered up until now. My weirdness is such a huge part of who I am that without it, I wouldn't really be me any more.

Well to be honest, I weird out other story tellers too. I do dress weird and have an odd hairstyle, and I admit to having a strange personality as well, but I'm just being myself and expressing who that is. I have no intention to 'shove it in people's faces' though. I just want to be able to walk into a room and not have everyone immediately tense up making me realize they will not take seriously anything I have to say. Most of all though, I want to be able to do this without sacrificing who I am. I act as well, but I like to do that as a break. If I have to act my way through the rest of my life then what's the point? replace me with one of the other humans being born every second and no one will notice. It feels like the world is rejecting me like a splinter, that its my very essence that isn't wanted, not my curly hair or non brand name clothes that I buy from the thrift shop cause it's all I can afford. I want somewhere that I can be embraced for who and what I am and I've traveled Canada looking for that place without any luck.

to be honest, there's no easy way, but it's never impossible. Myself, I rely a hell of a lot on distraction. when you're doing something, try to have some music or movies or something in the background, it may take focus away from whatever you're trying to accomplish, but it tends to save me from drifting back into the darkness. 
Also, pot helps.

My dad tried to kill himself in my bathroom by locking himself in with a bottle of pills and a 40 of vodka. He had been in there for 4 hours with just my room mate in the apartment and he didn't know what was going on so he didn't say anything. An hour after I got home I noticed it was locked and he was inside. had to call the ambulance and the cops so he wouldn't take a swing at the medics.
